label_suggestions.name: cloud-ok
label_suggestions.description: Issue can be validated, fixed, and re-verified in Codex cloud from repo state plus setup.

label_suggestions.name: validate-only
label_suggestions.description: Issue should stop after validation evidence and a scoped proposal instead of an unattended fix.

label_suggestions.name: needs-human-review
label_suggestions.description: Issue involves UX or product judgment and should not be closed by an unattended worker.

label_suggestions.name: requires-live-model
label_suggestions.description: Issue depends on live AI output and cannot be claimed fixed from fallback-only validation.

label_suggestions.name: local-only
label_suggestions.description: Issue depends on local-only assets, device-specific state, or context not reproducible in Codex cloud.

label_suggestions.name: needs-acceptance-proof
label_suggestions.description: Issue can be fixed in cloud but still needs a final local/browser-backed acceptance recording.

current_batches.description: First cloud wave: validation-first tasks for onboarding, HUD clarity, and CJK handling before any subjective fixes are approved.
Second cloud wave: trace-heavy interaction and transition issues after the first lane settles.
Cross-cutting cleanup after the focused fixes land.

issue_overrides.reason: Cloud can capture evidence and prepare a proposal, but onboarding flow and language-selection changes still require product judgment before an unattended fix.
The requested looping backdrop and avatar work are asset-dependent until shared asset hosting exists.
Cloud can reproduce the Block Crush HUD issue, but visual hierarchy and mobile clutter need human design review before a fix is accepted.
HUD discoverability is reproducible in cloud, but unattended copy or hierarchy changes should stop for human design review.
Broad readability cleanup should stay in validation-and-proposal mode until the narrower issues land and the final scope is agreed.
The issue is cloud-fixable, but a fixed claim requires direct evidence from live-model Korean output rather than fallback-only validation.
Cloud should trace and narrow the wasted-tap bug first; do not treat it as a simple unattended fix without issue-specific timing evidence.
The transition bug is reproducible in cloud, but it should remain a trace-and-propose issue until the stale-frame source is isolated.
Streaming behavior needs timing evidence first and should not be claimed fixed without player-visible progressive rendering proof.
